summary: The study investigates the influence of process parameters and pulse ratios of precursors on the characteristics of La1 − xAlxO3 films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films are deposited on p-type silicon substrates using trimethylaluminum (TMA) and tris(isopropylcyclopentadienyl) lanthanum as precursors, with H2O as oxidant. The optimal processing parameters are determined, including precursor heating temperature, deposition temperature, pulse time, and purge time. The results show that increasing the La precursor pulse ratio improves the film characteristics, such as dielectric constant, equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), and electrical properties. The study also highlights the importance of optimizing these parameters to achieve high-quality films with good surface morphology and reduced interfacial layer defects.
evidence: The influence of processing parameters of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) and lanthanum oxide (La2O3) gate dielectric is investigated. Trimethylaluminum (TMA) and tris(isopropylcyclopentadienyl) lanthanum [La(iPrCp)3] were used as precursors separately, and H2O was used as oxidant. The ultra-thin La1 − xAlxO3 gate dielectric films are deposited on p-type silicon substrates by atom layer deposition (ALD) for different pulse ratios of precursors. Effects of different La/Al precursor pulse ratios on the physical properties and electrical characteristics of La1 − xAlxO3 films are studied. The preliminary testing results indicate that the increase of La precursor pulse can improve the characteristics of film, which has significant effects on the dielectric constant, equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), electrical properties, and stability of film.
